idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe exactly the right cause or point of a situation
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the project was running out of time.
origin: Refers to a carpenter striking a nail squarely so that it goes straight into the wood

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a loud, angry complaint
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about accuracy in identifying something, not about complaining or getting angry

wrong_meanings.meaning: to fail completely at a task
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes success in being precise, so it means the opposite of failing
Nothing about construction or beginning a project is implied; the focus is on accuracy

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' comes from carpentry and means that someone has identified the exact cause or main point of a situation. It is often used in discussions and opinion essays to praise a precise argument.
